introHeading: The mirror booth, built for Westchester's estate and country club circuit
introParas: Westchester weddings and galas tend toward the kind of venue where the room itself is doing a lot of the decorating — a historic estate in Tarrytown, a country club in Scarsdale, a river-view space in Rye. The magic mirror's gold frame and full-length format sit comfortably in that setting rather than competing with it, and the touchscreen's animated prompts keep guests engaged whether it's a Bar Mitzvah crowd or a formal wedding party.

Those same venues are usually the strictest about vendor paperwork — a certificate of insurance naming the venue, a confirmed load-in window, sometimes a vendor meeting ahead of the date. We carry a $3 million policy and turn a COI around the same day you send us the venue's contact, which is exactly the kind of requirement Westchester's historic estates and country clubs tend to have and one we're used to clearing without being chased for it.

Setup takes about 20 minutes once we're in the room and we arrive a full hour ahead of your start time, same as anywhere else in our service area. The booth wants a 10ft x 10ft footprint, or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance where a room runs tighter, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet. Travel to White Plains, Yonkers, New Rochelle, Rye and the rest of Westchester is quoted from your venue's ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Mirror Photo Booth in Westchester — FAQ

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to bring the mirror booth to Westchester?
faqs.a: There's no flat borough-style rate the way there is closer to Brooklyn. Travel to Westchester is quoted from your venue's exact ZIP code before you book, so you see the real number up front.

faqs.q: Our country club requires a certificate of insurance naming the venue — can you provide one?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us the venue's contact — this is close to routine at Westchester's country clubs and historic estates, and we're set up to handle it quickly.

faqs.q: Does the mirror booth fit at a historic estate venue, or does it clash with the setting?
faqs.a: The gold frame and full-length format tend to sit well in a historic room rather than compete with it — it reads as an addition to the decor, not a piece of tech dropped into a period space. We're happy to send photos from similar Westchester venues if that helps you picture it.

faqs.q: How much space does the mirror booth need at a Westchester venue?
faqs.a: The optimal footprint is 10ft x 10ft, which leaves room for the backdrop, props table and a red carpet if you want one. We can compress to a minimum of 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for a tighter room, and we need one standard 110V outlet within 15 feet.

faqs.q: Is an attendant included with a Westchester mirror booth rental?
faqs.a: Yes. A trained attendant runs the booth for the full length of your rental — setup, keeping the prop table organized, helping guests use the touchscreen, and packing down at the end of the night.

faqs.q: Can the mirror booth be set up at a river-view venue in Rye or Tarrytown?
faqs.a: Yes, indoors or on a covered terrace. If the setup is outdoors we need level ground, shade for the touchscreen and a dedicated power run — river-view venues often have specific load-in and vendor rules, so we coordinate directly with the venue's event coordinator ahead of time.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and can you arrive early for a Westchester event?
faqs.a: Setup takes about 20 minutes once we're in the room, and we arrive a full hour before your scheduled start time so everything is tested and quiet before guests arrive. If your venue needs us on site earlier than that, idle time runs $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Which Westchester towns do you cover?
faqs.a: We're regularly out across White Plains, Yonkers, New Rochelle, Rye, Scarsdale, Tarrytown and the surrounding areas. If your venue isn't on that list, ask anyway — we'll tell you honestly whether we can get there.
